response.title: which enclosed 3d printer is the fastest at printing abs
response.answer:
For printing ABS as fast as possible, I'd prioritize an enclosed CoreXY printer with an actively heated chamber.

ABS is different from PLA: a printer advertised at 1,000 mm/s isn't necessarily faster at producing usable ABS parts. Chamber temperature, volumetric flow rate, acceleration, and cooling all affect actual print time.

The fastest printer on paper may not be the fastest at producing dimensionally accurate, warp-free ABS parts.

Best alternative for large ABS parts, with 30,000 mm/s² claimed acceleration and a 390 × 390 × 340 mm build volume.

One important distinction: the FLSUN S1 Pro advertises 1,200 mm/s, but lacks an actively heated chamber. I would not select it solely for that speed when ABS is the priority. 
Desktop 3D Printers
+1

I haven't found controlled, identical-model ABS print-time benchmarks sufficient to declare a definitive real-world winner.

One question: Are you trying to print ABS as fast as possible for small parts (under 100 mm) or large parts (200–350 mm)? That could change which printer is actually fastest for you.
